Teynham Parochial Church of England Primary School - Breakfast and After-School Provision
pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After-School Provision
At Teynham Parochial Church of England Primary School we offer both a Breakfast Club and Afterschool Club to help provide care for students outside of school hours.
Breakfast Club is run from 7.45am to 8.45am Monday to Friday. Breakfast will be served at 8.00am with a choice of cereals, fruit juice, fruit and toast. After breakfast the children will have an opportunity to play games, do colouring and other activities. We will ensure that they go to their classroom safely and on time for registration. It costs £3.50 per session.
After School Club is available from 3.15pm/3.20pm to 4.30pm Monday to Friday. There will be a charge of £3.00 for any child that attends and is collected by 4.00pm(£2.00 if in receipt of pupil premium) and £3.50 till 4.30pm (£2.50 pupil premium).
For further information on booking places please contact the school office on 01795 521217 or pop in and speak to a member of staff.

pageCache.text:
SEN - Special Educational Needs
We are committed to providing a fully inclusive environment. We believe that all children have the right to succeed and we aim to meet the individual needs of our pupils at all times. We are able to provide a range of interventions and strategies which will minimise barriers to learning in a fun and stimulating manner.
We hold the same expectations for pupils with special educational needs as for those without but remain fully aware that some children require a different approach in order to achieve success.
Click here to view our SEN Policy
The MIDAS centre (part of Meadowfields school in Sittingbourne) run a range of courses for parents and carers, many of which are free! The courses are run by specialists with a huge amount of experience and are always very popular. Please see our SENCO if you would like any further information or help with booking.

pageCache.text:
Governors
School governors are people who want to make a positive contribution to children’s education. Governors are one of the largest volunteer forces in the country and have an important part to play in raising school standards. The role of the governing body is absolutely key to the effectiveness of a school, each governor has a responsibility which relates to the School Improvement Plan (referred to as SIP). Monitoring Pair visits will relate to priorities and will be evaluated on the School Improvement Plan. It has been decided that Teynham Governing Body will be made up with 12 governors operating under the Circle Model, represented as follows:
Governor 2023 to 2024 information PDF File
Governor 2024 to 2025 information DOCX File
Mrs E Pearson - Head Teacher, Forest School Leader and Governor
I became headteacher of Teynham CE Primary School in September 2009.
Learn, Enjoy, Grow, our school motto, is fundamental to ensuring that all our children are given the best possible opportunities to succeed in all they do. I am proud to lead a hard working and dedicated team of staff who go ‘above and beyond’ every day. There are no business interests declared and earnings are less than £100,000.
Ms S Whittaker - Vice Chair of Govenors
A Local Authority appointment on the 30.01.20 term of office four years, whose attendance over the last year is 100%. A declared a business interest as a Sole Trader of a Local Catering Company, and does not earn over £100,000. Mrs Whittaker is responsible for Safeguarding, Health and Safety Quality of Teaching and Learning.
Governor Action Plan – Responsibility from SIP: Outcomes for children and learners
Mrs C Tomsett - Foundation Governor
I have been a Foundation Governor since 2019.
I have worked in early years for over 30 years at nurseries and preschools as deputy manager and then manager/owner.
My children had many happy years at Teynham Primary School and I’m keen to see that continue for the current roll, especially as we expand.
I love cats, reading, singing and signing.
Mrs Stratton - Co-opted Governor
I’m Miranda and I am a co-opted governor. I started the role in September 2022 when I stepped up as Manager of Teynham Community Preschool. My monitoring role is EYFS as I have experience in this field.
In my spare time I enjoy days out with my family or curling up with a book. I am also a leader at the local brownies group.
Mr D Parker - Parent Governor
Hi, I’m Dan, a parent governor and been in roll since November 2022. I am fortunate to have 2 children in the school setting, both currently in Key stage 1. I became a school governor as I fully believe in the school’s ethos and support all it stands for where the children’s happiness and education are the forefront of every decision. I feel my experience as parent and a manager at a large utility company can bring value to the roll and knowing my views and opinions are always held in high regard enables me to contribute in the decisions around the running of the school. My responsibilities and focus are on Health and safety and Pupil Premium.
Mr A Gregory - Parent Governor
‘Hello! I’m Adam and I’ve been a Parent Governor since November 2022. I have two wonderful daughters who attend the school and love it. I am a big believer that we continue to create an environment where our children can learn within a culture of acceptance, build resilience and flourish in unique ways. I love the fact that the vision and ethos of the school is underpinned by key Biblical values. One of the main parts of my role is to oversee Attendance at the school. As a governing body we look to ensure that as each child attends, it gives them best opportunity to ‘Learn, Enjoy and Grow’.’

Headteacher's Welcome (Vision)
Learn, Enjoy, Grow
“I am able to do all things through Him who strengthens me”
Phillippians 4:13
I am very proud to welcome you to Teynham Parochial Church of England Primary School. I hope you find our website interesting and informative giving you a taste about the wonderful things that happen in our school. We are a welcoming, inclusive school and we understand the importance of working in partnership with parents; we encourage parental involvement in children’s learning, as well as fostering opportunities for children themselves to be actively involved in their own learning.
We cultivate a rich environment in all we do so that the school community, have the right to Learn, Enjoy, Grow, developing spiritually and having awe-inspiring learning experiences. Our children learn within a culture of acceptance, build resilience and flourish in unique ways, underpinned through the teachings of Jesus, through God and in his world.
As Headteacher, I feel privileged to be leading this school and to be working with such a motivated and talented group of staff and governors.
Discover more about how our children enjoy their learning and time at Teynham by arranging a visit through our school office. I would be delighted to show you around our wonderful school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Teynham Parochial Church of England Primary School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
We aim to meet the needs of all children in the school by providing a broad and balanced curriculum, delivered through quality first teaching and by making reasonable adjustments where necessary. As a staffing body, we want all children to experience success and build upon their strengths and develop resilience and compassion.
Curriculum Maestro is our online platform which has an ambitious Primary Curriculum following National Curriculum objectives. The creative topic-based curriculum provides sequence and interconnection, while including the knowledge and skills needed. It comprises of, Science, Art and Design, Design Technology, as well as Maths and English. We also use the big ideas to make connections of previous learning and aid deeper thinking.
In addition to this, we cover Computing, Music and French is our Modern Foreign Language. We promote positive emotional health and help children develop social and emotional skills through PSHE. The Kent Diocese curriculum is used for RE.
Click here to view the school’s curriculum 2024
To underpin our curriculum, we use a set of 10 big ideas. These provide a purpose for the skills and knowledge chosen for each area of the curriculum. Children can then link the big ideas to previous learning with meaning. The big ideas form a series of inter connecting threads, allowing children to encounter and revisit their learning. Over time, this may help children to build conceptual frameworks and aid deeper thinking, with a more sophisticated understanding of information and ideas.
The children are introduced to the big ideas in Year R. They will continue to encounter them in all areas of learning as they continue on the educational journey through our school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Teynham Parochial Church of England Primary School - Accelerated Reader
pageCache.text:
Accelerated Reader
The children in our school show a great enthusiasm for reading and we want children to develop positive lifelong reading habits. Reading is taught through a structured approach. For early readers the book is matched to the phonic sound they are learning. As children’s reading develops they then start to use Accelerated Reader.
Accelerated Reader motivates, monitors and manages children’s’ independent reading practice helping them to develop a true love of reading. Click here to login into your child’s account.
This programme is supplemented with a wide assortment of attractive books of different genres. As the children progress through the school, they are introduced to literature of increasing complexity. They learn to analyse and evaluate a wide range of texts. Our well stocked children’s library introduces our children to the widest possible selection of books.
We believe that children become confident and fluent readers when both school and home support them. We encourage parents to hear their children read a little every evening and record comments in a reading record.

Forest School
Forest School helps to increase our pupil’s confidence, problem-solving and self-esteem through exploration, team building and encourages them to learn how to access and nurture the environment. At Teynham we have been running a Forest School for the past 7 years. All year groups from Year 1 to Year 6 have the opportunity to take part in a six week program every academic year.
School for Nature Award 2025-2026 The school recently received an award from Sir David Attenborough recognising it’s contribution to nature. Below is the award with Mrs Swann.
RSPB Wild Challenge March 2026 Rabbit, Dormouse, Robin, Owl, Otter and Hedgehog Classes all received a bronze certificate from the RSPB for taking part in the Wild Challenge, which recognises the help our school gives to local nature. Click here to view the certificates.
New additions to the Forest School family We are delighted to announce the arrival on Thursday 5th March two new members of our school’s Forest School team. Huge Henry and Little Leo the hedgehogs were kindly donated to the school by Hogwinkles Faversham and have already made firm friends with some of our year 6s.
